claim.pdf_says: 14.9.14.3   Syntax rules  (bold run-in heading, one level below '14.9.14 EXIT statement', same level as 14.9.14.1 General and 14.9.14.2 General formats)
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.14.3 Syntax rules   (H2 - while '### 14.9.14.1 General' and '### 14.9.14.2 General formats' are H3 and the parent is '## 14.9.14 EXIT statement')
claim.why_it_matters: Same defect: the EXIT syntax rules become a sibling of the EXIT statement rather than a child. Compare 14.9.15.1-.4 (FREE statement), which is correctly '## 14.9.15' + '### 14.9.15.N'.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides, with corrections to how it was described. PDF side: rendered p.654 at 300dpi - the page opens with a standalone bold heading line '14.9.14.3 Syntax rules', then FORMAT 1 / rule 1), FORMAT 2 / rules 2)-7) with sub-items a)-d) under 5). Rendered p.653 to establish the sibling typography: '14.9.14 EXIT statement', '14.9.14.1 General' and '14.9.14.2 General formats' are all standalone bold heading lines in the SAME face, size and weight as '14.9.14.3 Syntax rules' on p.654. The PDF therefore gives no typographic level distinction among .1/.2/.3 - they are peers, and the four-component number 14.9.14.3 is definitionally a child of 14.9.14. Markdown side: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27016 '## 14.9.14 EXIT statement', 27019 '### 14.9.14.1 General', 27032 '### 14.9.14.2 General formats', 27061 '## 14.9.14.3 Syntax rules', 27110 '## 14.9.14.4 General rules'. So .3 and .4 are emitted at the SAME depth as their own parent while .1 and .2 sit one level deeper. The claimed comparator is also accurate: 14.9.15 FREE is '## 14.9.15' + '### 14.9.15.1/.2/.3/.4' (lines 27155-27173), as is 14.9.16 GENERATE, so this is not a deliberate transcription convention - the file contradicts itself. Adversarial checks that did NOT sink the claim: the prose is complete and faithful (every rule 1)-7) and a)-d) on the page is transcribed with no dropped text, so this is not a text-loss finding hiding behind a heading); it is not page-break furniture (the level error is not caused by the 653/654 break - 14.9.13.3 and 14.9.13.4 are mid-page and equally mis-leveled); the anchor '' is present and correct, so link-based citation still resolves. Heading depth in Markdown is document structure, not cosmetic formatting: a consumer that extracts 'everything under ## 14.9.14' by reading to the next H2 terminates at 14.9.14.3 and silently drops both the Syntax rules and the General rules for EXIT - the exact failure mode that matters for spec-lookup section extraction. That is a genuine structural discrepancy, so real=true.
verdict.corrected_description: The finding is real but was mislabelled and under-scoped on three counts. (1) kind='missing-heading' is wrong - no heading is missing. The heading text, number and anchor are all present and correct; the defect is the heading LEVEL (H2 emitted where H3 is required), i.e. a heading-depth error. (2) The PDF characterization 'bold run-in heading' is wrong - on p.654 '14.9.14.3   Syntax rules' is a standalone bold heading on its own line, typographically identical to '14.9.14.1 General' and '14.9.14.2 General formats' on p.653; nothing runs in with the following text. The correct PDF-side evidence is the identical heading style shared by .1/.2/.3, not a run-in. (3) The scope is far larger than one page. 14.9.14.4 General rules (line 27110) carries the identical defect, and a sweep of all 255 headings under 14.9 found 43 mis-leveled - overwhelmingly the '.3 Syntax rules' / '.4 General rules' pairs (14.9.1.3/.4, 14.9.2.3/.4, 14.9.4.3, 14.9.10.4, 14.9.11.4, 14.9.12.4, 14.9.13.3/.4, 14.9.14.3/.4, 14.9.18.4, 14.9.19.4, 14.9.20.4, 14.9.22.3/.4, 14.9.23.4, 14.9.24.4, 14.9.25.4, 14.9.26.4, 14.9.27.4, 14.9.28.3/.4, 14.9.30.3/.4, 14.9.37.3/.4, 14.9.38.4, 14.9.39.3/.4, 14.9.40.3/.4, 14.9.44.3/.4, 14.9.48.4, 14.9.49.3, and more). A second variant runs the other way at 14.9.1, where the parent is '### 14.9.1' and the children are '#### 14.9.1.1/.1.2'. This should therefore be ledgered once as a systemic heading-depth normalization pass over ISO_COBOL.md (derive the hash count from the dotted section number), not as a per-page EXIT-specific finding. Severity 'structural' is right but the blast radius is bounded: no prose is lost and the dotted number inside each heading still carries the true hierarchy, so grep- and anchor-based citation is unaffected; only heading-tree/subtree navigation breaks.
